economic_question: Can a one-shot nonterminal release of already-open aggregate exposure at a causal sampled-equity drawdown trigger cut the damaging open-risk path while preserving enough later original profit to beat the qualified anchor inside 20% native equity DD?

new_mechanism.name: one-shot nonterminal open-exposure release
new_mechanism.trigger_state: first post-arming sampled equity DD from all-time sampled equity high
new_mechanism.excluded_reason: the recorded first-trigger snapshot has zero open lifecycle exposure

counterfactual.release_economics: realize the released fraction of aggregate marked floating P/L at the recorded trigger and subtract $25
counterfactual.affected_future_close: retain only the declared fraction of each affected lifecycle's frozen actual/stressed close economics
counterfactual.doubled_cost: preserve the full observed cost drag across released and retained fractions
counterfactual.transition_equity_envelope: until the last affected original close, charge min(-$25, final candidate-minus-baseline delta); afterward apply the exact final delta to sampled actual/stressed equity
counterfactual.interpretation: a conservative fixed-path proxy, not candidate-specific MT5 proof

selection_gates.profit: after the embedded $25 action reserve and an additional $50 uncertainty reserve, actual and doubled-cost-stressed net must each strictly exceed qualified observed +$1,691.54 / +$1,626.26
selection_gates.epochs: all four modified actual and stressed epoch nets must be positive
selection_gates.capital: actual/stressed closed balances and sampled equity envelopes must remain positive
selection_gates.drawdown: max(qualified native 19.550371765% + 0.25 points, worse conservative sampled equity DD + 0.193561860 points + 0.25 points) <= 20%
